clue.text: Places echo after shell goes off in coup

parts.note: to place something is to put it, so places gives puts

indicators.note: once the outer casing of the word echo is removed only its two inner letters are left

explanation.surface: A shell explodes, its echo carrying through a country in the middle of a military takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after shell goes off' strips the first and last letters from 'echo', leaving its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden violent seizure of government is called by this German-derived word, a direct synonym of the French loanword.

clue.text: Masses of cord beneath window displaying ad suddenly cut

indicators.note: in a down clue the cord piece sits below the window piece
suddenly cut means abruptly stopped, losing the final letter

parts.note: a pop-up is a browser window that appears showing an advertisement
a lace is a cord or string used to tie shoes

explanation.surface: A cord hangs below a window showing an advertisement that suddenly disappears.
explanation.definitionFit: The general public, the ordinary people of a country taken together, are the common masses.

clue.text: Kick or pull by the ears

indicators.note: by the ears says the word is judged as heard, by its sound

parts.note: to tow is to pull a vehicle or boat along

explanation.surface: A choice between kicking someone or dragging them by their ears.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick something lightly with the tip of the foot is to strike it with a digit of the foot.

clue.text: Isolate with bollards made of carbon something unique

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
a one-off is something made or done only once

explanation.surface: Someone describes a unique creation made from carbon, protected by bollards.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadworkers close off a lane by setting out traffic markers, which is what this verb phrase describes.

clue.text: Cancel exercising to grab a pill

indicators.note: exercising sets the words to grab a working, putting their letters through their paces into a new order

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, the drug taken as a pill

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their workout to reach for a tablet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercising' reads as a workout but signals the rearrangement; 'pill' is the usual crossword hint for the drug ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrogate a law or agreement is to repeal or annul it formally, a synonym for calling it off.

clue.text: In which one's not pulled out all the stops to relax?

definitions.text: In which one's not pulled out all the stops to relax?

parts.words: In which one's not pulled out all the stops to relax?
parts.note: a bus driver on leave still rides around, calling at every stop, so the break is like the job

explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled out all the stops' means made every effort, but here it is a driver pulling away from each bus stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday spent doing much the same as one's ordinary work, as a bus driver might on a coach trip.

clue.text: Steer mayor around contradictory parts of speech

parts.note: a steer is a young castrated bull, an ox

indicators.note: around says the letters of mayor are moved about

explanation.surface: A mayor is steered around by a contradictory speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb; it is the bullock. 'around' signals the rearrangement rather than a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures of speech joining contradictory terms, as in deafening silence, are the plural of this Greek word.

clue.text: Girl, one endlessly indisposed, couldn't stand without becoming wiped out

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside places the first piece around the second

parts.note: if you couldn't stand something you hated it

indicators.note: endlessly removes the final letter

parts.note: indisposed means unwell or ill

explanation.surface: A girl, constantly unwell, could not stand without being exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'endlessly' trims the synonym for indisposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Annihilated means destroyed utterly; wiped out is an informal phrase for the same total destruction.

clue.text: Yank wanting first to secure business degree to get on board

indicators.note: to secure means to hold firmly, so the piece holds the degree inside
wanting first means lacking its opening letter

parts.note: to yank is to pull sharply, to jerk
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: An American, needing first to get an MBA, sets out to win a place on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American; it is the verb. 'wanting first' leaves ERK, which goes round MBA.
explanation.definitionFit: To go aboard a ship or aircraft is to board it, so this verb means to get on.

clue.text: Woman who does very small parts lacking a high passion for film

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a cleaner, a woman who does for an employer

indicators.note: lacking says the letter for a is missing

parts.note: iotas are tiny amounts
meat that is high has gone off
ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: A woman who does tiny bit-parts lacks the passion for film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman who does' is British for a cleaning lady, a CHAR; 'lacking a' takes A from IOTAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1981 British movie about two athletes at the 1924 Olympics, an example of the general category.

clue.text: Shepherd's fired up with this hopeless ideal?

parts.note: shepherd's pie is the minced-lamb dish topped with mashed potato, so shepherd's suggests the dish
something fired up has been launched high overhead, up among the clouds

explanation.surface: A shepherd launched skyward seems an absurd picture of an unrealisable dream.
explanation.walkthrough: SHEPHERD'S PIE is a British dish of minced lamb under mashed potato; the question mark flags that a pie is only one kind the word could name.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a pleasant prospect that will never actually come about, a fanciful promise of future bliss.

clue.text: One who's rolling round in pain, numb finally

indicators.note: in places the round letter inside the pair of final letters
finally takes the closing letter of each of the words pain and numb

parts.note: a round shape is a circle, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone writhes in agony until finally going numb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who's rolling' means rolling in money; the surface makes it a person rolling about in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A nob is British slang for a wealthy upper-class person, someone rolling in it, that is very rich.

clue.text: One using catchy line female poet's finished off

parts.note: a lass is a girl or young woman
poets shorten over, meaning finished, to the contracted form o'er

explanation.surface: A woman poet wraps up her work with a memorable line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catchy line' is a rope that catches animals, not a memorable lyric.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone throwing a noosed rope to catch cattle or horses is using a line designed to catch.

clue.text: Healthier drink served from tank in style

indicators.note: served suggests the letters of tank in style are dished up in another order

explanation.surface: Drinks are served from a tank in stylish fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffee made with skimmed milk has fewer calories, so it is the more health-conscious choice.

clue.text: A different answer, his?

parts.note: something that is his is, by implication, not hers, giving not her

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a different answer might be his.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'his' only implies NOT HER.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means one more or one of a different kind, the same as saying a different one.

clue.text: Busy high up on arch, painting

parts.note: arch as a prefix means principal, as in archenemy, so chief
a Constable is a painting by John Constable, English landscape artist

explanation.surface: An artist is up on an arch, busily painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' is slang for a police officer, so a busy high up is a senior one; a CHIEF CONSTABLE heads a British police force.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a regional British police force is the most senior officer, a policeman at the top of the hierarchy.

clue.text: Informed article — paper regularly runs one?

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of paper

parts.note: the one who runs a paper is its editor, ed, so runs one becomes is ed

explanation.surface: A newspaper article regularly informs readers about someone it runs.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the twist: whoever runs a paper 'is ed', the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To be apprised is to have been told or made aware of something, a formal synonym for informed.

clue.text: To hand over service, make fresh poster

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
nones is a church service, the office said at the ninth hour
to make or perform something is to do it

indicators.note: fresh signals the word poster made anew, its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a church service and designs a new poster for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Nones is the canonical office said at the ninth hour, about 3pm; 'fresh' signals the rearrangement of poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close by, within easy reach of where you live, is to hand; the idiom means very near.

clue.text: One unexpectedly does right in America

indicators.note: unexpectedly says the letters of one turn up in a surprising order

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or swindle them, to con

explanation.surface: Someone surprisingly does the right thing in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' looks like a verb of doing right; it means swindles.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoconservatives are a hawkish faction of the American political right, shortened to this informal plural.

clue.text: Old police shield, very neglected, about to make comeback

indicators.note: about turns the assembled pieces round so they read backwards

parts.note: the RUC, Royal Ulster Constabulary, was the Northern Ireland police force until 2001

indicators.note: neglected says the letter for very is left out

parts.note: to cover something is to shield it

explanation.surface: An old police shield, long neglected, is about to return to service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neglected' takes V from COVER, leaving COER; 'about' turns RUCCOER right round.
explanation.definitionFit: To happen again after a gap is to come back, so this verb means making a return.

clue.text: Pair on the Jumbo wasting sec-ends? Shame!

indicators.note: pair says the piece appears twice, as an elephant has two tusks
wasting sec-ends means losing the second letter, the u

parts.note: a tusk is found on an elephant, Jumbo being the classic name for one

explanation.surface: Someone scolds an elephant for wasting time.
explanation.walkthrough: Each TUSK loses its second letter to give TSK, and 'Pair' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A clicking noise of disapproval, written as this pair of syllables, is an interjection meaning shame on you.

clue.text: West-facing ornamental buildings one disposed of following cheap sale

indicators.note: disposed of means thrown away, removing the letter for one
in an across clue, facing west means reading right to left, so the word is turned round

parts.note: follies are decorative buildings with no practical purpose built in country estates
one is the Roman numeral I
F is the abbreviation for following, as in ff in references

explanation.surface: West-facing garden follies are sold off, one at a bargain price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West-facing' turns FOLLIES into SEILLOF; 'disposed of' removes I, leaving SELLOF, then F.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale of goods or shares at a low price to get rid of them quickly is a disposal at knockdown rates.

clue.text: Minor derailment buries fitting

indicators.note: buries says the letters lie concealed within the run Minor derailment

explanation.surface: A small train derailment covers some fittings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fitting is appropriate or proper, and the phrase means correct and as it should be.

clue.text: Worthless stuff one's left old director

indicators.note: left here means has departed, so the letter for one goes from the name

parts.note: Jacques Tati was a French film director of the mid twentieth century
one is the Roman numeral I; one's stands for one has

explanation.surface: Someone says a veteran director has left behind only rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's left' reads as one has left: I leaves TATI.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap tasteless goods or junk are commonly dismissed by this informal British word for rubbish.

clue.text: Where a few lead moulds lie, chairs go

indicators.note: moulds reshapes the letters of lie, chairs go into a different form

explanation.surface: In a foundry, lead is moulded where chairs are discarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like the metal beside 'moulds'; it is the verb of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: States governed by a small ruling group are by definition places where power rests with the few.

clue.text: Square in ancient Rome, the base for predatory woman

parts.note: four is a square number, two squared, and the Roman numeral for it is IV

indicators.note: in a down clue the base of a word is its last letter, here of predatory

explanation.surface: A square in ancient Rome serves as the hunting ground for a predatory woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'predatory woman' looks like the definition; only 'woman' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is a woman's given name, like other plant names such as Holly and Hazel.

clue.text: Sculptor drops in in military cap, mainly to conform

indicators.note: the second in places one piece within the other
mainly means most of it, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: a kepi is a French military cap with a flat top and peak

indicators.note: drops says the following word is let fall out of the name

parts.note: Jacob Epstein was a modernist sculptor working in Britain

explanation.surface: A sculptor pops in wearing a soldier's cap so as to fit in.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the two 'in's, the first is what the sculptor drops and the second is the container signal; 'mainly' trims the cap.
explanation.definitionFit: To march in time with others is to stay in line, and figuratively means conforming to what everyone does.

clue.text: Took revealing picture of adult, with yen for smut finally

indicators.note: for says one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: an adult film is one rated X, giving x-rated

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word smut

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for the yen, Japanese currency

explanation.surface: Someone with a yen for smut snaps a racy picture of an adult.
explanation.walkthrough: Y replaces T, the last letter of 'smut', in XRATED.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiograph shows the inside of the body, so taking one is literally capturing a revealing image.
